subject: Operational assurance: temporary uptime uplift request & credit escrow mechanics
messages:
From: Anna Ruiz <anna@heliopay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Brooks <sam@heliopay.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Operational assurance: temporary uptime uplift request & credit mechanics

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — HelioPay is ready to move to production next month, but we have one remaining concern from our ops and finance teams. During onboarding we've seen higher-than-expected traffic bursts and want to lock in a stronger short-term availability commitment while we complete our scaling tests.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provisionally commit to 99.99% uptime for the first 90 days post-go-live (we expect go-live ~Oct 1)?
- If the higher uptime is agreed, can we limit the monthly service-credit exposure to a capped amount (HelioPay prefers a cap equal to 10% of monthly spend) and have the remainder go into an escrow/holdback to be reconciled after the pilot?

I've attached our SLA request PDF and a usage snapshot. We appreciate a quick response — legal is standing by for an amendment if we can agree to terms.

Best,
Anna Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure
HelioPay

Attachments: HelioPay_SLA_request_v2.pdf, usage_snapshot_sep.csv
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Anna Ruiz <anna@heliopay.com>
Cc: Sam Brooks <sam@heliopay.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 18:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational assurance: temporary uptime uplift request & credit mechanics

Hi Anna — thanks for the detail and for sharing the snapshot. Congrats on the go-live milestone.

Short answer: we can propose a structured option that balances your need for a provisional uptime uplift with Redwood's operational and financial guardrails. I'll loop in our product/legal briefly and follow up with a concrete term sheet.

Initial thoughts (high level):
- 90-day pilot where Redwood will allocate a dedicated pool and target a provisional 99.99% availability for the pod serving HelioPay.
- Service-credit calculation remains per the SLA (minutes of downtime -> credit percentage), but we can:
  - cap monthly credits at 10% of the invoice for the pilot term, and
  - hold excess credit value in an escrow/credit ledger for reconciliation at the end of the pilot (applied to future invoices or one-time true-up).
- To make the uplift sustainable, we would expect a modest committed-minimum consumption for the pilot or a short-term capacity addendum (details to propose).

I'll propose precise credit math and an amendment draft by EOD tomorrow. If HelioPay's legal wants to pre-read a term-sheet, I'm attaching a provisional term sheet draft.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow morning to walk through the numbers?

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_provisional-term-sheet.docx
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: HelioPay SLA uplift request — internal proposal

Laura / Aditya — forwarding Anna's note and our draft. High level ask: temporary 99.99% for 90 days with a monthly credit cap at 10% and escrow for excess. They explicitly prefer escrow instead of immediate payout.

Operational constraints / suggested guardrails (what I recommend we offer):
- Offer the provisional 99.99% but only on a Dedicated cluster (isolated pool) to avoid cross-customer risk.
- Monthly credit calc: keep existing per-SLA minute -> % mapping, but apply a monthly cap at 10% of HelioPay's monthly invoice for the pilot. Any amount above the cap is recorded as 'escrowed credits' on HelioPay's account and can be used as a billing credit at the end of the pilot (or rolled forward).
- Escrow funding mechanics: we do not pay out actual cash; we record credits that reduce future invoices or are netted at the pilot close — this avoids cash flow risk for Redwood while giving HelioPay protection.
- Operational pre-reqs: HelioPay must agree to (a) a minimum committed capacity for the pilot (30 days' equivalent) OR (b) an advance deposit equal to one month of committed spend to cover rapid provisioning.
- Canary ramp: start with 48-hour production canary, then scale to full traffic for the remaining 89 days. If we see sustained overload, the uplift can be rescinded with 72h notice to HelioPay.

Question for legal/finance: is the escrow-as-credit construct acceptable from Amortization / revenue recognition POV? Aditya — do you want to take a quick look at the proposed cap language and confirm finance is ok with credit-led escrow?

If we can agree internally, I'll send a polished amendment to Anna and propose a DocuSign route.

— Naomi
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Anna Ruiz <anna@heliopay.com>
Cc: Sam Brooks <sam@heliopay.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational assurance: temporary uptime uplift request & credit escrow mechanics — proposed pilot amendment

Hi Anna — thanks for the patience. Attached is our proposed pilot amendment (summary below). If this aligns, we can run DocuSign and target a Sep 30 effective date.

Summary of proposed pilot amendment (90 days):
- Uptime: Redwood will provision dedicated capacity and target provisional 99.99% availability for HelioPay for the first 90 days following the effective date. This is an operational target tied to Dedicated pool SLAs; it is provided as a limited-term amendment.
- Monthly service credits: standard SLA credit math applies (per-minute buckets -> percentage of monthly service fee).
- Monthly cap: service credit payouts are capped at 10% of the monthly invoice for the duration of the pilot. Any credit value above the cap is recorded in an escrow ledger on HelioPay's account.
- Escrow mechanics: escrowed credit is non-cash; it is applied to subsequent invoices or reconciled at pilot close. If unused after reconciliation, it may be applied as a one-time invoice credit per the amendment.
- Preconditions: HelioPay to commit to one of: (A) a 30-day committed minimum consumption level, or (B) an advance equivalent to one month's committed spend.
- Canary & termination: 48h canary window; Redwood may revoke the provisional uplift with 72h notice in case of systemic overload or behaviour outside of agreed usage patterns.
- Cap on total liability: separate from the monthly cap, Redwood requests a maximum cumulative service credit exposure during the pilot equal to 30% of projected 90-day spend (to protect against extreme events).

Links & next steps:
- Draft amendment (DocuSign): https://app.redwood.com/docusign/HV-9832-amendment
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HV-9832

If this looks reasonable to HelioPay, please let me know and we will route legally for signature. Happy to jump on a call later today if Anna or Sam want to walk through any item.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
